description:
A craniofacial surgeon needs to document the cranial vault angle from a CT Cranium scan for pre-operative cephalometric analysis.

The CT Cranium dataset is already loaded in InVesalius. Using InVesalius's ANGULAR measurement tool (the protractor/angle tool, NOT the linear distance ruler), place at least one three-point angular measurement on the skull anatomy.

Suggested approach: In the sagittal view, place three points along the curvature of the cranial vault (e.g., one point on the frontal bone, one at the vertex, and one on the occipital bone) or at the skull base to measure an anatomical angle. The measured angle should be anatomically reasonable — between 30 and 170 degrees.

After placing the measurement, save the project to:
/home/ga/Documents/cranial_angle.inv3

IMPORTANT: Use the ANGULAR measurement tool (protractor icon), not the linear measurement tool (ruler icon). The angular tool requires placing THREE points to define an angle.
